articles.title: A Deeper Look at Sunspots
articles.summary: The article "A Deeper Look at Sunspots" explains sunspots as deep, dark, and semi-transparent depressions on the Sun's surface, detailing the Wilson Effect and the scientific reasons for their appearance. It attributes their darkness to suppressed convection by strong magnetic fields and their semi-transparency to lower temperature and density. The author also emphasizes the enhanced viewing experience of sunspots, especially in 3D using H-Alpha telescopes, and provides a detailed activity calendar for the San Jose Astronomical Association for September and October 2012.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky
articles.summary: This article discusses the lunar multi-ring Orientale basin, detailing its formation theories, visibility due to libration, and a comparison with Mercury's geology. It also provides an observing guide for September, highlighting the positions of various planets and a unique "appulsar" event on September 23rd where Uranus makes a close approach with the star 44 Piscium, offering a rare opportunity for naked-eye and binocular observation.

articles.title: A Brand New Age: Queue Observing at Mt. Paranal
articles.summary: The article describes the author's visit to the Mt. Paranal observatory in Chile, highlighting its modern "queue observing" system. This method involves resident astronomers specializing in instruments and collecting data for other scientists, a stark contrast to traditional individual observing. The author emphasizes the system's increased efficiency, collaborative nature, and environmental benefits, despite a personal reflection on a potential loss of observing romance.

articles.title: Fixit Program
articles.summary: The SJAA Fixit program offers free telescope repair, tune-up, and setup assistance to club members and attendees on the first Sunday of each month at Houge Park, alongside the SJAA Solar Observing program. Recent activities included collimation, GOTO function setup, new telescope assembly, and repairs for the advanced scope loaner program. Members needing help are encouraged to contact the program in advance via the SJAA website.

articles.title: ASTRONOMY magazine renewal time
articles.summary: Jim Van Nuland is organizing the group renewal for Astronomy magazine subscriptions for the 2013 year. Subscribers can renew at a special group rate of $34 for one year or $60 for two years by sending a check to him. Independent subscribers can convert to the group rate, and new subscribers can also join, with all checks to be held until late September.

articles.title: The Last Month In Astronomy
articles.summary: The last month in astronomy saw the successful landing of the Mars Science Laboratory 'Curiosity' on Mars using innovative sky crane technology. Tragically, America's first woman in space, Sally Ride, passed away at age 61. Additionally, the Spitzer Infrared Space Observatory detected a candidate for the smallest exoplanet discovered to date, UCF-1.01, orbiting its star every 1.4 days.

articles.title: If You're Reading This - We Want You!
articles.summary: The article, penned by SJAA President Mark Wagner, serves as a direct appeal for members to volunteer, contribute new ideas, and actively participate in the astronomy club's growth. It showcases several successful new programs like Solar Observing, Fix-It Day, an Imaging SIG, and Quick STARt for beginners, demonstrating the club's adaptability and welcoming attitude towards new initiatives. Wagner emphasizes that the club's vibrancy stems from member involvement and encourages attendance at board meetings to help shape its future.

articles.title: It Must Be Astronomical...
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) has revamped its telescope loaner program, introducing "QuickSTARt" for new astronomers. The article details the successful completion of two school star parties in July 2012 and lists 8 more scheduled for the 2012/2013 school year. Additionally, it provides contact information for SJAA officers, staff, and publication details for their monthly newsletter, the Ephemeris.
